pages.name: 05 Operations and decisions
pages.title: Operations | Ownership, assumptions, and design gaps
pages.subtitle: Design review prompts, not proof of security, availability, or compliance. Service configuration and requirements must be confirmed.

nodes.label:
REFERENCE ASSUMPTIONS

One region; no disaster recovery design.
Separate workload subscriptions.
Azure-provided DNS for clients.
Private zone centrally owned.
Private endpoint shown in Spoke 1.
No implicit spoke-to-spoke transit.

ROUTING AND SECURITY DECISIONS

Confirm CIDRs and non-overlap.
Enable required peering traffic settings.
Define firewall rules and subnet routes.
Use specific prefixes for inspected transit.
Check symmetric return paths.
Private endpoint inspection needs its own design.

OWNERSHIP AND OPEN QUESTIONS

Platform team: hub, firewall, shared DNS.
Workload teams: apps, subnets, endpoints.
Define public access and admin access.
Choose sizes, zones, region and budgets.
Define recovery objectives and retention.
Hybrid access is a separate extension.

Azure Firewall
Diagnostics enabled by configuration

VALIDATION BEFORE DEPLOYMENT
Confirm effective routes, firewall allow/deny behavior, private DNS answers, public access settings, and least-privilege permissions.
A default route alone does not force more-specific private endpoint or peering traffic through the firewall.
If cross-spoke access is required, design explicit routing and inspection. Do not treat peering as transitive.
